question: Should OpenClaw include this dependency-bearing WhatsApp phone-code flow once the branch is conflict-free and the shared auth/session behavior is physically verified?
rationale: The feature is member-sponsored and well-shaped, but accepting a new shipped dependency plus changes to existing QR and persisted-session behavior is an explicit compatibility and release choice that automated review cannot make.

options.title: Approve after gates
options.body: Resolve conflicts, authorize the exact dependency head, and require physical-device fresh-login and upgrade-path proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow compatibility surface
options.body: Keep phone-code pairing but avoid shared browser-identity or auth-lifecycle changes that cannot be proven necessary across QR and existing sessions.

options.title: Pause inclusion
options.body: Retain QR-only login until maintainers are ready to own the dependency and session-compatibility burden.

recommendation.title: Approve after gates
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, authorize the exact dependency head, and require physical-device fresh-login and upgrade-path proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows the strongest direct ownership of the affected WhatsApp socket and credential lifecycle, and this decision spans compatibility and release acceptance.
